questions.stem: How many odd days are there in a leap year?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Normal year = 365 days = 52×7+1 → 1 odd day. Leap year = 366 days = 52×7+2 → 2 odd days. 'Odd days' = extra days beyond complete weeks. These are key to finding the day of the week.

questions.stem: If today is Monday, what day will it be after 100 days?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 100 ÷ 7 = 14 remainder 2. So 100 days from Monday = Monday + 2 days = Wednesday. **Short Trick:** Divide by 7, take the remainder. Add remainder to the starting day: Mon(1)+2 = Wed.

questions.stem: January 1, 2020 was a Wednesday. What day was January 1, 2021?
questions.explanation: C is correct. 2020 is a leap year (divisible by 4, and by 400 check: 2020÷4=505 exactly ✓). Leap year = 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 odd days. Jan 1, 2020 = Wednesday. Jan 1, 2021 = Wednesday + 2 = Friday.

questions.stem: Which of these years is NOT a leap year?
questions.explanation: C is correct. LEAP YEAR RULES: (1) Divisible by 4 = leap year. (2) EXCEPTION: Divisible by 100 but NOT by 400 = NOT a leap year. 1900 is divisible by 100 but NOT by 400 → NOT a leap year. 1600, 2000, 2400 are divisible by 400 → ARE leap years. 2024 ÷ 4 = 506 (no remainder) → leap year.

questions.stem: How many Sundays are there in the month of February 2021 (not a leap year)?
questions.explanation: B is correct. February in a non-leap year has exactly 28 days = 4 complete weeks (28÷7=4 with no remainder). Every day of the week appears EXACTLY 4 times. So there are exactly 4 Sundays. (In a leap year, February has 29 days = 4 weeks + 1 day, giving some days 5 occurrences.)

questions.stem: If 15 March 2023 was a Wednesday, what day was 15 March 2022?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 2022 is a normal year (365 days = 1 odd day). 15 March 2023 is Wednesday. Going BACK 1 year (through 2022's 365 days): subtract 1 odd day. Wednesday − 1 = Tuesday. (Going forward through a year adds odd days; going backward subtracts them.)

questions.stem: A month starts on a Friday. What is the maximum number of Sundays it can have?
questions.explanation: B is correct. If the month starts on Friday (day 1), the first Sunday is day 3 (since Friday+2=Sunday). Sundays: 3, 10, 17, 24, 31 — but day 31 exists only if the month has 31 days → 5 Sundays. But question says starts on FRIDAY: day 1=Fri, day 2=Sat, day 3=Sun — first Sunday is day 3. If month has 31 days: Sundays on 3,10,17,24,31=5. Maximum = 5.

questions.stem: Today is Thursday. A project deadline is in 50 days. On what day is the deadline?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 50 ÷ 7 = 7 remainder 1. Add 1 day to Thursday: Friday. **Quick reference:** Day codes (0=Sun, 1=Mon, 2=Tue, 3=Wed, 4=Thu, 5=Fri, 6=Sat). Thursday(4)+1=5=Friday.

questions.stem: The last day of February in a leap year falls on a Saturday. What day does March 1 of that year fall on?
questions.explanation: B is correct. In a leap year, February has 29 days. If Feb 29 (last day of February) is Saturday, then March 1 is the very next day = Sunday. Simple consecutive day problem.

questions.stem: How many total odd days are there in 400 years?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 400 years in the Gregorian calendar = 97 leap years + 303 normal years. Total days = (97×366)+(303×365) = 35,502+110,595 = 146,097 = 7×20,871 exactly. 146,097÷7=20,871 with remainder 0. So 400 years = exactly 20,871 weeks with 0 odd days. This is why the Gregorian calendar repeats every 400 years.
